vibe: Patch-Tuesday energy on a Wednesday — active Windows IKE exploitation leads, Copilot keeps getting jailbroken, and Mojo just went open source.

cyber.title: Critical Windows IKE Extension RCE — now actively exploited
cyber.summary: CISA confirms in-the-wild exploitation of a critical RCE in the Windows IKE extension. Corroborated by a broader alert flagging macOS, SharePoint, and vCenter flaws under active attack too. If you run any Windows infra, this is patch-now.

cyber.title: Copilot keeps getting jailbroken — 3 separate disclosures
cyber.source: Ars Technica + The Hacker News + Dark Reading
cyber.summary: A cluster: Microsoft Copilot revealed the hidden input that let it be hacked; separate 'CoSnitch' attack tricked Copilot into mapping out internal architecture; and a one-click prompt-injection flaw could exfiltrate data from Copilot Personal. The AI-assistant-as-attack-surface story is now a weekly fixture.

cyber.title: MLflow SSRF flaw exploited to steal cloud credentials
cyber.summary: Attackers are abusing an SSRF bug in MLflow (the ML lifecycle platform) to pull cloud credentials and secrets. Notable because it sits right at the AI/ops boundary — your ML tooling is now part of the attack surface.

cyber.title: Medusa ransomware hit 500+ critical-infrastructure orgs
cyber.summary: CISA puts a number on Medusa's spread: 500+ critical-infra victims. Scale story more than a new-technique story, but the IOCs in the advisory are worth a glance if you're defending.

cyber.title: 'Ransom Busters' — ransomware crew poses as an incident-recovery service
cyber.summary: A cheeky twist: an actor claims to have hacked other ransomware servers and is shaking down those victims 'to help them recover' for up to a hefty fee. Social-engineering meta-layer on top of the usual extortion.

cyber.title: StopAndProtect: ~2,000 hacked WordPress sites spreading malware
cyber.summary: Fake 'protection' campaign weaponizing ~2k compromised WordPress sites. Standard-but-sizable web-malware op; relevant if you run WP anywhere.

ai.title: Mojo is now open source
ai.summary: Modular (now under Qualcomm) open-sourced Mojo — the Python-superset language built for high-performance AI/systems work. Big deal for the AI-infra crowd; a genuinely fast Python-family language going open changes the calculus for a lot of ML tooling.

ai.title: AI 'mind viruses' can spread between agents via persistent prompt files
ai.summary: Research on self-propagating prompt injections that hop between AI agents through shared/persistent prompt files. Early-days threat model, but this is exactly the direction agentic-AI security is heading — worth knowing the term.

it.title: China-linked actor demonstrates AI-assisted capabilities in APAC attack
it.summary: State-linked group showing off AI-augmented tradecraft in a regional (APAC — relevant to you, Tom) intrusion. Signal that the 'AI in offensive ops' era is operational, not theoretical.

videos.title: How to install Qubes OS and replace Windows (step by step)
videos.verdict: WATCH — if you want a genuinely hardened daily driver
videos.summary: Clean, complete walkthrough of installing Qubes OS (the VM-isolation security distro Snowden, Mullvad and the EFF all endorse) over Windows — hardware requirements, making the Rufus USB, the install itself. High signal for a tutorial. Verdict: watch if you're tempted to run a security-first machine; skip if you're not switching OS — the summary tells you what it is and who it's for.

videos.title: What should security leaders do with AI? They don't know.
videos.verdict: SKIM — the takeaways are here, skip the panel
videos.summary: IBM X-Force panel podcast. Core advice: start AI in your red teams and on repetitive L1/L2 alert triage to fight alert fatigue — don't over-reach. Cites that 64% of orgs still make limited/no use of AI in security. Also touches 'ghost jacking' and whether AI is any good at patching. Decent but low signal density — ~20 min for 3 takeaways.
